_comment: IN-5 coverage ratchet baseline. CI fails if measured coverage drops below these minus the tolerance in scripts/check-coverage.mjs. Raise these numbers (never lower) as coverage improves to lock in gains. Regenerate the measured values with `npm run test:coverage`. QW-3 (2026-07-17): re-baselined from a real coverage run (77.45/68.45/70.81/80.20) — the previous numbers were half the actual coverage and the ratchet could never fire; a ~0.5 pp margin below measured absorbs v8 attribution jitter beyond the checker's own tolerance. UX review (2026-07-27): the batch's new error/loading branches first dropped branches to 67.35% and failed this gate; covering them with real tests for UserMenu (sync-status row, favorites row actions, GDPR export/delete) and Legend (grid badge/error/loading/filter captions) took a measured run to 77.98/69.22/71.44/80.81, re-baselined here with the same ~0.5 pp margin. Data-honesty pass (2026-07-27): measured is now 77.64/69.49/71.27/80.41 — LOWER on statements/functions/lines than the run above despite adding tests, and that is expected rather than a regression. ShortlistTray.tsx had never been imported by any test, so v8 reported it with statements.total === 0 and it was absent from the denominator entirely; the first test that renders it added its 143 statements / 117 branches / 38 functions to the total. Adding a partial first test for any untested file therefore always pushes this ratio DOWN, which makes the ratchet actively penalise the work it exists to encourage — the gate compares a ratio whose denominator it does not control. Covering the tray properly (42.6% -> 63.6% statements) is what put the numbers back over the floor. The thresholds below are deliberately NOT raised to the new measured values: the next file to gain its first test will move the denominator again.
